name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,437

clue.text: Increase rapidly when everyone's in favour

indicators.note: the word for everyone is placed inside the word for a favour

blocks.note: everyone is all
a boon is a favour or blessing

explanation.surface: Support for something snowballs once everyone backs it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'everyone's in favour' reads as unanimous approval, but it is ALL placed in BOON, giving BALLOON.
explanation.definitionFit: Prices or debts that balloon swell quickly, like a bag being inflated with air.

clue.text: Happen to find fish on board as well

indicators.note: on a ship means aboard it, so the fish goes inside the vessel

blocks.note: to be is to take place or happen
SS, steamship, is the usual crossword vessel to be on board
the ide is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: Someone happens to discover a fish on a boat too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' is the crossword convention of going inside SS, a steamship; 'Happen' is BE in the sense of take place.
explanation.definitionFit: Besides is an adverb meaning in addition or also, alongside what was mentioned.

clue.text: Made up lie about debut of Real's left-winger

indicators.note: something made up is invented, so the letters are put together afresh
a debut is a first appearance, so only the initial letter is wanted

blocks.note: taken as written
first letter of Real

explanation.surface: A fabricated story about a Real Madrid winger's first game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left-winger' sounds like a footballer at Real Madrid; here it is a political supporter.
explanation.definitionFit: A Labourite supports the British Labour Party, traditionally on the political left.

clue.text: Plainly apparent in extra time

blocks.note: over means extra or left over
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Something becomes obvious only once a match goes to overtime.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt means done openly and visibly rather than secretly or hidden.

clue.text: Wrong over having to prevent access to space inside military housing unit

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means turned upside down, so the word reads backwards
the printer's space goes within the word for preventing access

blocks.note: a sin is a wrong
to shut something is to close it off
an en is a printer's unit of space

explanation.surface: Something wrong with locking soldiers out of their quarters.
explanation.walkthrough: An en is a typographic space half the width of an em.
explanation.definitionFit: A Nissen hut is a prefabricated half-cylinder corrugated iron shelter used by the armed forces.

clue.text: Avoid being last to get away

blocks.note: food that lasts keeps
to be off is to leave or get away

explanation.surface: Someone avoids coming last in a race by escaping early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last' looks like a position in a race but is the verb meaning to endure.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep off a subject or a substance is to steer clear of it entirely.

clue.text: Dairy products reportedly made by people in northern Iraq

indicators.note: reportedly means as said out loud, so the word is judged by its sound

blocks.note: curds are set milk solids, as in curds and whey

explanation.surface: Cheese and yoghurt said to be made by Iraqi farmers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kurds are an ethnic group whose homeland includes northern Iraq, Turkey, Syria and Iran.

clue.text: Choose line penned by Lincoln to show what Labour may have become

indicators.note: something penned is enclosed as in a pen, so one piece is held inside the other

blocks.note: to elect is to choose
L is the abbreviation for line
Abe is Abraham Lincoln's short name

explanation.surface: A line written by Lincoln is chosen to show how the Labour Party has changed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penned by' looks like authorship but means L is enclosed by ABE.
explanation.definitionFit: A party that has become electable is one voters might now choose to put in government.

clue.text: Relating to former times as happy without a bit of gloominess

indicators.note: without means lacking, so a letter is removed
a bit of a word is a single letter of it, here the first

blocks.note: first letter of gloominess
golden as in happy times, a golden age

explanation.surface: Nostalgia for the past as a cheerful time with no gloom.
explanation.walkthrough: GOLDEN loses its G to give OLDEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Olden is an archaic adjective meaning of a bygone era, as in the olden days.

clue.text: Send on an attacker

blocks.note: first meaning: to pass mail on to a new address
second meaning: an attacking player in football or rugby

explanation.surface: A manager sends a striker onto the pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Letters are redirected to a new address, and in team sports the attacking players are called by this name.

clue.text: Black bishop residing in northern town

indicators.note: someone residing in a town lives within it, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: B is the chess notation for bishop
Sale is a town in Greater Manchester, in the north of England

explanation.surface: A dark-skinned or black-robed cleric lives in a town up north.
explanation.walkthrough: B goes inside SALE to give SABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Sable is the heraldic term for black, also used poetically for the colour.

clue.text: Deliver over split boarding, having no doubt - right?

indicators.note: a passenger boarding a ship goes inside it, so one piece is put within the other

blocks.note: to rend is to tear apart or split
someone sure has no doubt
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A doubtful question about whether a split is coming on board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deliver over' is the whole definition; 'having no doubt' and 'right' combine to make a comparative meaning more certain, which the split boards.
explanation.definitionFit: To surrender something is to hand it over or relinquish it to another party.

clue.text: Probably hypocritical to stock earliest of tomes on saints

indicators.note: a shop stocks goods by holding them within, so one piece sits inside another
earliest means only the opening letter of the following word is wanted
in a down-style reading, one piece is placed after the other, so this joins them in order

blocks.note: double-dealing or two-faced, as in a double life
opening letter of tomes
SS is the abbreviation for saints

explanation.surface: A two-faced bookseller keeps religious books about saints.
explanation.walkthrough: Hypocritical is double in the sense of double-dealing; 'on' in a down-style reading places the saints after the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Doubtless is used loosely to mean very likely, as in 'doubtless you have heard'.

clue.text: Country cousin's bottom seen through loose flowing garment

indicators.note: the bottom of a word is its final letter
something visible through a garment lies within it

blocks.note: last letter of cousin
the toga was the loose robe of ancient Rome

explanation.surface: A rustic relative's backside is visible through a baggy robe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country cousin' looks like a single phrase, but Country is the definition and cousin supplies its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonga is a Polynesian kingdom of islands in the South Pacific Ocean.

clue.text: Stylish cane

blocks.note: first meaning: smart and fashionable
second meaning: as a verb, to beat or flog with a stick

explanation.walkthrough: 'cane' looks like a fashionable walking stick but is the verb for beating.
explanation.definitionFit: Swish is informal for posh and elegant, and also means to strike with a whipping stick.

clue.text: Powerful heroin's what the arrogantly superior may be on

definitions.text: what the arrogantly superior may be on

blocks.note: high as in high-powered or strong
horse is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: Strong drugs are what snobs are high on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' plays on being on drugs; the idiom is to be on one's high horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on their high horse behaves with self-righteous arrogance, looking down on others.

clue.text: Destined to join obscure set

indicators.note: one word is attached to another, so the two are written side by side

blocks.note: to obscure is to hide
bound to happen means destined

explanation.surface: Someone fated to become part of a little-known clique.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' looks like a group of people, but it is the definition: set in one's ways.
explanation.definitionFit: A hidebound person is rigidly conventional and unwilling to change, fixed in their views.

clue.text: Cultural decline in North Carolina initially evident after the 30's for instance

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the next word
the state and letter come after the time span, so they are placed second

blocks.note: the thirties is an example of a ten-year span
NC is the postal abbreviation for North Carolina
first letter of evident

explanation.surface: Signs of moral decay were noticed in a southern US state in the 1930s.
explanation.definitionFit: Decadence is moral or cultural deterioration, typically marked by excessive indulgence.

clue.text: In complete agreement with peacekeepers over containing hostility? Just the opposite

indicators.note: containing says one piece holds another inside it
this flips the stated containment, so the holder and the held swap roles

blocks.note: United Nations troops keep the peace
animus is hostility or ill will
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: Peacekeepers overcome hostility to reach consensus, or not.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, 'over containing hostility' puts ANIMUS inside O; 'Just the opposite' reverses that, so O goes inside ANIMUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Unanimous describes a decision shared by every member, with no dissenting voices.

clue.text: Quote about Green movement at first showing great vitality

indicators.note: movement suggests the letters of the colour word shift around
about means turned round, so the word for quote is read backwards
the shuffled colour word is placed at the front of the answer

blocks.note: taken as written
to cite is to quote

explanation.surface: A quotation about the environmental movement in its early days was full of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green movement' looks like environmental politics but splits into the word and its anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An energetic person is lively and active, displaying plenty of strength and drive.

clue.text: Dean oddly ignored song's charm

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters are left out, so only the even ones remain

blocks.note: second and fourth letters of Dean
a chant is a song or sung phrase

explanation.surface: A cathedral dean strangely disregards the choir's singing.
explanation.definitionFit: To enchant is to delight or bewitch someone, as if casting a spell.

clue.text: Insist upon being strict

blocks.note: first meaning: to demand and obtain
second meaning: precise and rigorous

explanation.surface: Someone demands that rules be enforced rigorously.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to demand something from someone; as an adjective it means precise or rigorous.

clue.text: Capable of being stretched in future possibly to include the centre of Basildon

indicators.note: the grammatical word includes the selected letters within it
the centre of an eight-letter word is its fourth and fifth letters

blocks.note: the future is an example of a verb tense
the two middle letters of Basildon, a town in Essex

explanation.surface: An Essex town's centre might be stretched by future development.
explanation.definitionFit: Tensile describes a material able to be drawn out or extended under tension.

clue.text: Fasten on to bag

blocks.note: first meaning: to secure with a latch
second meaning: to capture or seize, as a hunter bags game

explanation.surface: An instruction to clip something onto a handbag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bag' looks like a handbag but is the verb for capturing.
explanation.definitionFit: A door catches when its latch engages, and a fielder or hunter catches what they capture.

clue.text: Understood to be essentially unskilled in diplomacy

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its central letter
the central letter goes inside the word for diplomacy

blocks.note: middle letter of the nine-letter unskilled
tact is diplomacy

explanation.surface: Someone is fundamentally incompetent at diplomacy.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacit describes something implied or understood without being openly stated.

clue.text: Version of text revealing communist infiltration primarily in part of Ealing

indicators.note: primarily means first, so just the opening letter is taken
the selected letter is placed within the place name

blocks.note: red is the colour and nickname of communism
opening letter of infiltration
Acton is a district in the London borough of Ealing

explanation.surface: An edited document exposes a communist plot to infiltrate west London.
explanation.definitionFit: A redaction is an edited form of a document, or the act of preparing it for publication.

clue.text: Studies grass say at start of semester

indicators.note: say means as spoken, so the plant word is replaced by a word sounding the same
the start of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: a reed is a tall grass
first letter of semester

explanation.surface: A student studies grasses at the beginning of term.
explanation.walkthrough: To read a subject is British usage for studying it at university.
explanation.definitionFit: At a British university one reads a subject, meaning one studies it for a degree.

clue.text: Pick an irresistibly funny person first off

indicators.note: the first letter is taken off the word

blocks.note: a scream is a hilarious person

explanation.surface: Choosing a hilarious comedian to go first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pick' looks like a verb to choose; it is the noun, the best of a group.
explanation.definitionFit: The cream of a group is its finest part, just as the pick of the bunch is the best.

clue.text: Make sure of showing sectarian trouble

indicators.note: trouble suggests disorder, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Confirming evidence of religious unrest between factions.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascertain a fact is to find it out for certain by checking or investigation.

clue.text: Italian writer covering for the most part one cause of food poisoning

indicators.note: most of the word is kept, so its final letter is dropped

blocks.note: Umberto Eco wrote The Name of the Rose
a lid is a covering

explanation.surface: An Italian author wearing a covering is blamed for an upset stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: Umberto Eco, author of The Name of the Rose, is a favourite crossword Italian writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Escherichia coli is a bacterium whose harmful strains commonly cause illness from contaminated food.

clue.text: Stuff regularly found in orders for hats

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter, here the second and fourth
the chosen letters are located inside the word for orders

blocks.note: second and fourth letters of stuff
tiers are ranks or orders

explanation.surface: Hat-makers find stuffing material in their orders.
explanation.walkthrough: TITFER is Cockney rhyming slang for a hat, from 'tit for tat'.
explanation.definitionFit: Titfer is British rhyming slang, short for tit for tat, meaning a hat.

clue.text: Appreciate not starting without academics being all together

indicators.note: the word loses its opening letter
without in the old sense of outside, so one piece wraps round the other

blocks.note: to sense is to perceive or appreciate
MAs are holders of a Master of Arts degree

explanation.surface: A warning not to value something without all the academics present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, so it signals wrapping round, not leaving out.
explanation.definitionFit: En masse is French borrowed into English for in a single body, as a group.
